newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen keeping positive edge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen keeping positive edge.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to keep their upward momentum Wednesday on optimism spurred by a global bond issue, unexpectedly boosted Tuesday afternoon to $1.0 billion from $750 million, dealers said.

"The market will latch onto this good news to push higher," said Dario Lizzano at Banco Rio. "The important thing for investors today is to know how Argentina will refinance its debt, and they see that not only is money appearing, but at rates which are reasonably good long-term."
The global bond fetched a coupon of 11 percent at its pricing in London earlier Wednesday.
Traders singled out the steel sector as a buy opportunity based on recent strong industrial production data and good earnings forecasts.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index closed up 0.4 percent Tuesday at 560.99, continuing a steady four-week rise which notched up gains of 10 percent in September.
"If volume finally starts to grow then the MerVal should be able to knock down resistance at 561 and turn that into a support level," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
Floor volume remained weak at 13.6 million pesos Tuesday.

Traders said the market would shrug off weak fiscal revenue data for September, which according to official estimates released Tuesday fell 0.2 percent from the same month of 1995 when the economy was in recession.
